title: Retention proxy for per-route differential TTL, pseudonymized metadata preservation, and attested evidence exports
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Implement a retention proxy service that centralizes per-route TTL enforcement for prompts/responses/request logs/metrics, preserves pseudonymized request metadata required for audits, and produces cryptographically-attested evidence bundles on demand. The proxy will sit between ingestion (API layer / gateway) and downstream storage/telemetry sinks and should: (1) apply route- and tenant-scoped TTLs with policy inheritance and overrides, (2) create lightweight pseudonymized metadata (stable per-tenant pseudonyms + retention tags) for forensic lookups without exposing raw PII, (3) tier metrics and logs into hot/cold retention windows with sampled rollups to meet unit-cost and compliance needs, (4) support on-demand evidence exports with hash-chained manifests and signer metadata for legal/infosec requests, and (5) integrate hooks for the Console to preview simulated retention outcomes and drift alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy enforces per-route TTLs: route default, tenant override, and explicit request TTL respected and visible in request headers
Pseudonymized metadata created and persisted separately from full request payloads; pseudonyms are stable per-tenant and reversible only by KMS-wrapped tokens (key material not stored in proxy)
Metrics/logs tiering implemented: hot (90 days), warm (365 days aggregated), cold (7 years sampled) configurable per-tenant with default presets
Evidence export API returns an attested bundle (manifest + objects + signature) and includes a verifiable SHA-256 chain linked to the retention rule that triggered it
Console simulation shows expected deletes/aggregations for a sample tenant and flags retention drift where policy and actual retention diverge
End-to-end integration tests and a canary rollout to 10% of traffic with telemetry and rollback metrics defined
tasks: Design: define retention proxy API surface and schema for pseudonymized metadata (Priya)
Storage: add S3 prefixing/TTL index for proxy-managed artifacts (Mateo)
KMS: integrate key wrap for pseudonym reversibility and evidence signing (Security)
Batching: implement metrics aggregation pipeline with deterministic sampling for cold-tier (Telemetry)
Console: add simulation endpoint and UI hook for previewing retention outcomes (Product/Console)
E2E tests: create synthetic tenants and run retention, export, and restore flows (QA)
Runbook: document evidence export review process and legal hold procedure (Support)
Canary rollout and observability: dashboards for deletion rate, export rate, and drift alerts (SRE)
comments: 2025-11-06 Priya Kapoor: Initial ticket created after PM sync; scope focuses on prompts/responses/request logs/metrics and excludes binary attachments — iteration 1 will surface attachments as separate artifacts.

2025-11-08 Mateo Rivera: Spike completed for pseudonym strategy — we will use per-tenant stable pseudonyms generated with HKDF over tenant salt + request-id and encrypted with KMS to allow reversible lookup only via the key service. Draft design at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RET/Retention+Proxy+Design

2025-11-10 Security Review (Lena Ortiz): Requesting clarity on key rotation impact to existing pseudonym reversibility; recommended adding versioned key identifiers into evidence manifests so exported bundles remain verifiable across rotations.

2025-11-12 Engineering (Mateo): Implemented prototype for TTL header propagation and soft-delete markers (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4421). Observed 3% p99 latency increase on request path in local benchmark — plan to mitigate with async persistence and batched writes.
2025-11-14 PM feedback (Aaron Blake): Add a customer-facing retention preview in Console that can simulate how a change to a per-route TTL affects stored artifacts over a 30/90/365 day horizon.

2025-11-16 QA (Nina Patel): Found edge case when tenant override TTL is shorter than request TTL — proxy currently applies the longer TTL. Marked as blocker; fix in progress to ensure shortest applicable TTL wins.
2025-11-18 Mateo Rivera: Fixed TTL precedence bug and added unit tests. Preparing canary configuration and runbook. Waiting on Security for final key policy sign-off.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy proxy in read-only mode with simulation flags to 0% (feature gate off)
Stage 2: Enable soft-delete markers and simulation endpoints in canary cluster (10% traffic) for 72h
Stage 3: Enable enforcement for non-sensitive routes and monitor deletion/aggregation metrics for 7 days
Stage 4: Gradually expand enforcement to >=90% traffic and enable evidence export API
Stage 5: Full rollout and deprecation of legacy TTL enforcement in storage layer
notes: Trade-offs: We prefer a proxy that issues pseudonymized metadata to avoid modifying customer payloads and to centralize TTL logic. This increases coordination with storage teams but reduces cross-system drift. We will defer per-tenant bespoke sampling strategies to a later iteration to keep MVP scope manageable. Legal requested a cryptographic proof chain; we implemented a manifest format that records rule-id, key-id, and object hashes for each export.
